name: 5-amino-1MQ

track.title: Lab & animal
track.line: Mouse, rat and cell studies, 2018 to 2024

track.title: Research use only
track.line: Sold labelled not for human use; not FDA approved

what.text: 5-amino-1MQ (5-amino-1-methylquinolinium) is a small molecule, not a peptide. It blocks an enzyme called nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT). Researchers at the University of Texas Medical Branch developed this class of NNMT blockers, and a company founded by one of them, Ridgeline Therapeutics, has studied it in mice.

Dimet-Wiley A, et al. Sci Rep 2022

what.text: How it acts, according to animal and cell studies

items.text: NNMT adds a methyl group to nicotinamide, a form of vitamin B3; it is raised in fat and muscle in some diseases. In fat cells grown in the lab, NNMT blockers lowered the enzyme's product (1-MNA), raised NAD+ and SAM, and reduced fat build-up.

src.label: Neelakantan H, et al. Biochem Pharmacol 2018
Awosemo O, et al. J Pharm Biomed Anal 2021

items.text: In the 2018 study, the blockers did not inhibit related enzymes tested, and passed through cell layers in lab tests.

src.label: Neelakantan H, et al. Biochem Pharmacol 2018

items.text: In mice given it under the skin, it reached fat, muscle and liver.

src.label: Babula JJ, et al. Diabetes Obes Metab 2024

what.text: None of these effects has been measured in people.

research.text: No published human studies found as of November 1, 2026. Every study found was in mice, rats or cells, and most came from the group that developed it. ClinicalTrials.gov lists no trial.
PubMed searches for its chemical name returned 3 papers, none in people, and a search for '5-amino-1MQ' returned none. ClinicalTrials.gov searches for both names returned no trials.

research.title: NNMT blockers in obese mice and fat cells (Neelakantan et al.)

facts.v: lab tests of a series of methylquinolinium NNMT blockers, then an animal study of a potent one
mice made obese on a high-fat diet
body weight, white fat mass, fat-cell size, cholesterol, food intake

research.found: The blocker lowered body weight, white fat mass, fat-cell size and total cholesterol. Food intake did not change, and no adverse effects were seen. The abstract does not name the exact compound tested in mice.

src.label: Neelakantan H, et al. Biochem Pharmacol 2018

research.title: Muscle repair in old mice (Neelakantan et al.)

facts.v: animal study: saline or an NNMT blocker after a chemical muscle injury
24-month-old mice
1 or 3 weeks after injury
muscle stem cell activity, muscle fibre size, contraction strength

research.found: Muscle stem cell activity rose in treated mice. Muscle fibres in the injured muscle were nearly twice as large, and peak force was about 70% higher than in controls. The abstract calls the drug an NNMT inhibitor without naming the compound.

src.label: Neelakantan H, et al. Biochem Pharmacol 2019

research.title: Blood levels in rats (Awosemo et al.)

facts.v: drug-level study after a vein or mouth dose
rats
levels in blood and urine; half-life; oral absorption

research.found: About 38% of a mouth dose reached the blood. Half-life was about 4 hours after a vein dose and 7 hours after a mouth dose.

src.label: Awosemo O, et al. J Pharm Biomed Anal 2021

research.title: Diet change plus 5-amino-1MQ, gut microbes in obese mice (Dimet-Wiley et al.)

facts.v: animal study comparing obese mice switched to a low-fat diet with or without 5-amino-1MQ
mice made obese on a Western diet
gut bacteria in the cecum; body weight and fat

research.found: With the low-fat diet, treated mice lost weight and fat faster than mice on the diet alone and had a distinct pattern of gut bacteria.

src.label: Dimet-Wiley A, et al. Sci Rep 2022

research.title: Obese mice for 28 days (Babula et al.)

facts.v: animal study: vehicle or 5-amino-1MQ once a day; plus drug-level tests by vein, mouth and under the skin
mice made obese on a high-fat diet
28 days
body composition, blood sugar, insulin, liver tissue, liver enzymes

research.found: Treated mice gained less weight and fat, handled glucose better and had less fatty liver. 4 of the 5 authors are Ridgeline Therapeutics' founder or current or former staff.

src.label: Babula JJ, et al. Diabetes Obes Metab 2024

research.title: Old mice with and without exercise (Dimet-Wiley et al.)

facts.v: animal study: NNMT blocker, intensive exercise, both, or neither
mice from 22 to 24 months of age
about 2 months
grip strength, running, muscle force and size

research.found: Grip strength was about 40% higher in treated sedentary mice than in untreated ones, and about 60% higher with treatment plus exercise. The abstract does not name the compound.

src.label: Dimet-Wiley AL, et al. Sci Rep 2024

research.title: Cervical cancer cells (Akar et al.)

facts.v: lab study on HeLa cervical cancer cells and HEK-293 kidney cells; no people or animals treated
cell growth; cell-death signs; gene and protein changes

research.found: 5-amino-1MQ slowed HeLa cell growth and caused signs of cell death, without apparent effect on HEK-293 cells.

src.label: Akar S, et al. J Obstet Gynaecol 2021

research.text: A 2024 bladder cancer study used it in mice: it reduced tumour growth and added to the effect of an immunotherapy antibody. The human part of that study looked only at the NNMT enzyme in tumour samples; no person was given 5-amino-1MQ.

src.label: Yang M, et al. J Immunother Cancer 2024

us.text: 5-amino-1MQ is not FDA approved for any use. It is sold labelled 'for research use only' or 'not for human consumption'. FDA does not allow such products to be sold for human use. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: none. No approved drug contains it, and no human trial is registered.

src.label: ClinicalTrials.gov search for '5-amino-1-methylquinolinium'

items.text: FDA says it has warned companies that illegally sold unapproved drugs falsely labelled 'for research purposes' or 'not for human consumption' that were in fact sold to consumers for human use with dosing instructions. FDA said this about GLP-1 drugs; the same labels do not make any unapproved drug legal to sell for human use.

after.text: 5-amino-1MQ is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or the 2027 List. Class S0 bans at all times any pharmacological substance not covered elsewhere on the List and with no current government approval for human therapeutic use. Whether WADA applies S0 to 5-amino-1MQ was not confirmed.

side.text: Nothing is known about its side effects in people. No human study was found. Animal studies by its developers reported no observable adverse effects. No animal toxicity study was among the papers found.

items.text: in the 2018 obese-mouse study, the authors observed no adverse effects and no change in food intake.
